page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is a memory-intensive server belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 168.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. The server has no local storage and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2348.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds, such as 34.74 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, due to the low vCPU count, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2217.38 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2886.0. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with uncached large-block read speeds at 21.36 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides an extremely high density of memory relative to compute resources, making it a specialized option for workloads that require massive memory footprints but minimal parallel processing. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications that do not scale across many cores, such as large single-threaded database operations, caching layers, or memory-bound analytical tasks.
